caption: A glass of ice water sits on a wooden table in a warm room, and condensation runs down the outside of the glass onto the table.

sa.check: A glass of ice water stands on a wooden table.
Droplets cover the outside of the glass.
A wet ring forms on the table.
Ice is visible in the glass.
The droplets grow before they run.

pc.expect: The beading only builds while the glass stays cold: droplets grow, join and run, and the ring on the table only grows.
pc.fail: The droplets shrink or go while the glass stays cold with ice in it; or the ring on the table shrinks; or the glass beads and dries in turn; or the beading eases while the ice is still there.

pc.expect: Droplets that grow large enough run downward on the glass, leaving trails, and gather at its foot.
pc.fail: A droplet runs up the glass; or water gathers on the rim's top and stays; or a drop leaves the glass and rises; or a run travels sideways round the glass and stays level.

pc.expect: The water on the outside comes out of the air onto the cold glass, and the ring is fed by runs off the glass.
pc.fail: The glass's own level drops as the ring grows; or beads form on the inside of the glass; or the ring appears on the table with no water running down to it; or drops detach and drift off into the air.

pc.expect: The beads behave as water on glass: they stay rounded, merge when they touch and run as streaks, and the wood darkens where it is wet.
pc.fail: Touching drops overlap without merging; or drops jump about on the glass; or the beads turn to hard frost while the glass runs with water; or the table stays dry-looking under a spreading ring.

pc.expect: One glass on one table; the glass keeps its shape and nothing passes through it.
pc.fail: The glass changes shape; or a second glass appears; or the ice passes through the glass's wall; or the glass sinks into the table.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The table's grain away from the ring, the room and the glass's pattern stay the same.
pc.fail: The table's grain changes pattern; or the room's contents rearrange; or the glass changes pattern.
